overall: Committee violated the OML by approving its November 29, 2016 minutes late and by failing to periodically review executive session minutes; no violation on the November 15 minutes timeliness or accuracy.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 15, 2016 minutes were not approved in a timely manner after being moved, tabled, and revised over several meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Considering that the minutes were approved within the next two Committee meetings after being tabled, we find that the Committee approved the minutes in a timely manner and did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 29, 2016 minutes were not approved in a timely manner; the committee approved them only on February 28, 2017.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to the November 29 minutes, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by not approving the minutes until February 28, 2017.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 15, 2016 open session minutes inaccurately omitted the complainant's statement about the superintendent's contract extension.
allegations.key_passage: While the approved meeting minutes do not include reference to Schooldigger.com, they otherwise offer a concise summary of Mr. Soares' statements.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to periodically review executive session minutes to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements.
Caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
